newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA WEATHER-WHEAT LOOKS BETTER AS RAIN FALLS.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA WEATHER-WHEAT LOOKS BETTER AS RAIN FALLS.

text.p: More rain fell over the weekend in Australia's drought-hit eastern and southern grainbelt, with further falls forecast.
The rainfall, generally in the 10 millimetres range, has begun to switch market sentiment to a belief that wheat yields may be better than feared before last week's rainfall, brokers said.
Rainfall occurred widely throughout a band through most of South Australia, southwest Victoria and southwest New South Wales --- areas where it was badly needed.
Australia's Bureau of Meteorology continues to predict persistent dry weather throughout southeast Australia over the next three months because of the El Nino effect.
After the weekend rain, however, Sydney Futures Exchange wheat prices fell on Monday in early trading as the belief strengthened that yields would improve.
Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures described the weekend rainfall as "pretty good".
"Literally, every rural market now is totally weather driven," he said.
Last week SFE wheat was about A$200.00 a tonne but on Monday SFE wheat opened at about A$190.50 with the market backing off quickly, purely on weather, he said.

After good localised rain in South Australia, Victoria and southern NSW, weather charts were suggesting more rain to come with a general front moving through Victoria and likely to bring good general rain.
"We all wait now to see how good that general rain turns out to be."
But Australian markets remained on a knife-edge waiting for the reality of whatever weather systems brought, Booth said.
"We're all in this holding pattern, watch and wait, if the rain does eventuate the market will produce better yields and the Sydney market will fall by up to A$10.00 a tonne.
"All of a sudden the pressure in the grain market comes off," he said.
